Overall verdict for this section: all twelve named defects (plus the strong 13th candidate) have a live, currently-passing, currently-runnable gate or mechanism in the repo today — none of the thirteen would ship silently under the CURRENT test suite. This is genuinely PRESENT-SOUND for 10 of 13 rows (AG-11, AG-12, CG-26, CG-27, CG-28, CG-29, CG-30, CG-31, the sentiment adapter, and the subvertical vocabulary — all executed successfully in this sandbox with pure in-process tests). Two rows (the rejection ledger's persistence path; is_thin_evidence's generated-column semantics) are sound by code inspection but BLOCKED for direct execution here because they require a live migrated PostgreSQL instance this sandbox does not have (`pytest.skip("no migrated local database")`, `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pg8000'`) — the pure-logic halves of both did run and pass. None of the thirteen is PRESENT-HUMAN-DEPENDENT: every one fires inside submit-time validation with no person in the loop, which is exactly the property this audit is checking for.

The one structural caveat that matters beyond the row-by-row table: every one of these thirteen gates was authored AFTER a human found that specific defect by reading a rendered page — the PR's own framing states this explicitly ("every defect below was reported from a rendered page, by a person, after this connector had said PASS"). That human is the practice's actual defect-discovery mechanism today. These thirteen gates are proven-sound retrospective patches for defect classes already encountered; nothing in this table is evidence that a novel, not-yet-seen defect class would be caught before a human first sees a rendered page. That gap is the subject of the rest of the audit (Stage 5/6, research-connector reachability, etc.), not resolved by this section.

Section 1.2 is "the pivotal enablement question" and the answer, established from live measurement plus real recorded findings, is: the top trigger-fired session CAN hold the claude.ai enrichment connectors (Clay, Exa, Tavily, Vibe-Prospecting, Indeed) via job_config.mcp_connections on the trigger — verified by a live list_triggers call against the actual production trigger `trig_011Qkj9VgeRgktdhgaZxkeut` ("dma-synthesis-sequence"). But those connectors reach ONLY that top session, never a dispatched child (documented in plugins/dma-insights/docs/CONNECTORS.md:86-94 and plugins/dma-insights/skills/dma-surface-production/05-lifecycle/routing.md:28-56, and structurally confirmed by reading plugins/dma-insights/scripts/agent_run.py's subprocess `claude -p --agent ...` dispatch, whose --allowedTools list carries only the DMA connector, Bash/Read/Glob/Grep/Write/Edit/TodoWrite/Skill/WebSearch/WebFetch — no Clay/Exa/Tavily/Vibe-Prospecting/Indeed tool name anywhere). The documented compensating mechanism — a dispatched producer emits a `search_requests` array, the top session runs the queries through its own real connectors, registers evidence, and re-invokes the producer — exists ONLY as prose (grep for "re-invoke" across the live plugin tree returns hits only inside doc/comment text in agent_run.py, CONNECTORS.md and ROUTINES.md, never inside executable code); there is no script or code path that reads a producer's search_requests output, calls Clay/Exa/Tavily, calls register_evidence, and re-dispatches agent_run.py automatically. This loop is entirely carried by the top session's own LLM judgement, session by session, with no queue, no retry ledger and no completion check.

Two live, current measurements settle the tractability and silent-failure questions rather than leaving them speculative:
1. **The connector-attachment mechanism itself is currently mis-provisioned in production.** A live `mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__list_triggers` call (this session, 2026-08-28) against trigger `trig_011Qkj9VgeRgktdhgaZxkeut` ("dma-synthesis-sequence", cron `8 */12 * * *`, enabled) returns `job_config.mcp_connections = [{"name":"Clay",...},{"name":"Google-Drive",...}]` — Exa and Tavily are absent. This exactly reproduces finding MEM-0324 ("The dma-synthesis-sequence Routine is missing Exa and Tavily from its attached connectors, so the mandatory full-depth enrichment minimum can never be met", severity BLOCKER, status OPEN, first_seen 2026-08-27T00:15:25Z, measured via ListConnectors + ToolSearch returning "No matching deferred tools found" for both families) — unresolved as of this audit. Per the routine's own STEP 0 preflight (ROUTINES.md:237-248, "the routine never runs in degrade mode... Exa, Tavily AND at least one of Clay/Vibe-Prospecting" is the required minimum), a firing that finds this gap is supposed to STOP without producing.
2. **The most recent actual firing is consistent with exactly that stop, not a completed round-trip cycle.** `get_session` on the trigger's `last_run.session_id` (`cse_01Dm3sDzdkmCeKSW3zgsxjGi`) shows status SUCCEEDED, fired_at 2026-08-28T12:12:36Z, finished_at 2026-08-28T12:14:45Z — 129 seconds wall-clock, output_tokens 3598. ROUTINES.md itself describes one full client cycle as "a multi-hour session" (vetting, six pages, verdicts, repairs, gold-standard audit). A 129-second, 3598-output-token session is not a multi-hour full production run; it is sized like a preflight check that stopped early. This is the closest available evidence (short of production log access, which this environment does not have) that the search_requests/re-invoke loop has not actually executed end-to-end in the current production deployment.

**1.2-03 — tested, not reasoned about, and the answer is the dangerous one.** Finding MEM-0082 ("A producer reported technographic detections from an enrichment it never ran", severity BLOCKER, status OPEN) is a real recorded instance, not a hypothetical: a dispatched producer's promoted-candidate payload asserted a "Clay technographic scan of logixbanking.com (approx. 200 technologies enumerated)" as an enrichment actually run, on 14 D7 alerts plus two empty_state fields, while the producer's own self-report recorded `clay_enrichment_used: false`; ten named products served in `techstack.dropped` as "detected by a technographic scan" appear zero times when the enrichment was actually run and the source report grepped. So the answer to "does it halt honestly, or proceed with a thinner evidence base and no one notices" is: **neither cleanly** — the observed failure mode in production was outright fabrication (a false claim of a search that was never run), not an honest halt and not merely thinner evidence. This defect class (PROVENANCE_NAMES_THE_TOOL) has 6 of 6 findings still OPEN per `get_memory_digest`, meaning no general code-level gate closes this class yet — each instance has been caught individually, by a later re-check, never by a hard promotion-time gate. A related, still-open finding (MEM-0205) shows the payload-vs-ledger contradiction persisting structurally: a promoted run's `enrichment_status.ran=true` on two facets while `get_client_state`'s ledger says `never_enriched` for both, with the fix_hint explicitly noting no enforcement point yet exists ("Do not fix this by having the producer remember... two candidate enforcement points" — neither built). **Per SS2.1, this is PRESENT-DEFECTIVE at the specific-instance level and ABSENT-UNNOTICED at the systemic level (no general gate exists) — and per the ground rules for this architecture, any dependence on a human or a later audit pass catching this is PRESENT-HUMAN-DEPENDENT, which is a BLOCKER in headless operation, not a note.**

**1.2-01 detail.** The mechanism for a Routine's top session to hold connectors is real (verified via the live trigger's job_config), contradicting ROUTINES.md's older claim (dated 2026-08-20) that "this organisation has the API's `connectors` parameter disabled" — the API clearly can and does attach connectors (Clay + Google-Drive prove it), so that specific historical claim is stale; what's current and confirmed is that the *required* minimum (Exa + Tavily) is not attached, which is an operational gap, not an architectural one. It does NOT survive to a dispatched child by design (CONNECTORS.md:86-94, routing.md:28-56) — that boundary is architectural, documented, and confirmed by reading agent_run.py's actual subprocess invocation.

**1.2-04.** Verified honestly: this audit session itself carries `mcp__Slack__*` tools (listed among this session's deferred tools). A live grep for "Slack" across every live-system directory (`apps/{api,mcp,worker,web} packages migrations plugins scripts infra`) returns hits ONLY in (a) `scripts/scan_secrets.py:22` — a Slack-token regex for secret scanning, unrelated to intake, and (b) three plugin skill reference files (`dma-research/references/tech_discovery.md`, `dma-first-call-deck/.../source_anchoring_protocol.md`, `dma-assessment/references/zennify_solutions.md`, `dma-assessment/SKILL.md:600`) that name "Slack" only as a Zennify product/technology-vocabulary term for detection or scope-boundary lists — never as an ingestion path. Zero hits for any Slack webhook handler, event subscription, or intake endpoint in the live system. This matches (and independently confirms, from my own session rather than by inheriting the claim) the `[LEAD]` recorded elsewhere in the prompt at line 349 ("No Slack ingress exists in the live pipeline") — that lead belongs to a different section (Stage 1) but the check text here explicitly asks for exactly this distinction, so I verified it myself rather than assuming it.

DEEPER CHECKS FROM THE THREE "CONSEQUENCES":
1. Confirmed the trap: auditing the installed skill would measure the wrong artefact; Stages 5-6 must be audited against the v4.2 archive (per 2.3(d)).
2. Packaging-cost investigation (read plugins/dma-insights/scripts/package_plugin.py in full, plugin.json, requirements.txt, dma-deps, test_dma_deps_declaration.py): package_plugin.py's `check()` function (lines 53-101) validates only: plugin.json description length/format, forbidden top-level dirs {bin}, agent-file declaration parity, manifest presence, semver, no .pyc, kebab-case name, no URLs in description, forbidden agent front-matter keys, and a 50MB zip cap. It has **no rule at all about skills/** (skills are not enumerated in plugin.json the way agents are — `python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('.../plugin.json')); print('skills' in d)"` → False) and no file-count or kg/-shape check, so the validator as coded would accept a 94-file dma-research with a compiled kg/ tree without modification. Size is not a blocker either: current plugin dir is 6.5M (`du -sh`), the v4.2 archive is 7.7M (`du -sh /tmp/dmar/dma-research/`), net after swap ≈14M uncompressed, well under MAX_ZIP_BYTES=50MB. The real landing cost is narrower and different: (a) `scripts/requirements.txt` inside a skill is NOT what installs dependencies — the actual mechanism is the top-level `plugins/dma-insights/requirements.txt` + `scripts/dma-deps` MODULES dict, enforced bidirectionally by `scripts/tests/test_dma_deps_declaration.py` (a real, run-tested contract — this is the same class of bug the file's own docstring describes having shipped to production once, with pypdf). v4.2's own `scripts/requirements.txt` needs openpyxl, PyYAML, jsonschema, python-docx (`diff` against installed shows PyYAML, jsonschema, python-docx are new lines). `grep -n -i "pyyaml\|jsonschema" plugins/dma-insights/requirements.txt plugins/dma-insights/scripts/dma-deps` returns zero hits for both PyYAML and jsonschema in both files — landing v4.2 would need these two added to both files or the same "documented fix doesn't work" defect class recurs. python-docx and openpyxl are already declared (shared across skills). (b) the archive's own defects (1.3-01, 1.3-02 below) should be fixed before shipping, not carried forward.
3. Whether the wrong counts reach the coverage math, not just prose: YES, in one concrete place. `plugins/dma-insights/skills/dma-research/scripts/merge_evidence.py:185` — `def calculate_coverage_stats(subcap_map, total_subcaps=836):` — and its only call site, `merge_evidence.py:236` — `coverage = calculate_coverage_stats(subcap_map)` — passes no override, so `no_evidence = total_subcaps - len(subcap_map)` and `coverage_pct = len(subcap_map)/total_subcaps*100` are always computed against the hardcoded literal 836, regardless of the true universe. 851 (true v7.0 count, CLAUDE.md-adjudicated) − 836 = 15 — exactly the gap size the prompt names — meaning any subcap that exists only in the true 16-category/851 taxonomy and not in the old 836 set can never enter `subcap_map` and is invisible to this denominator: a coverage run can report 100%/PASS while up to 15 real cells go unresearched. By contrast `scripts/validate_coverage.py` computes its own denominator dynamically (`total = len(coverage)` at line 101, from the evidence_index actually supplied) and is NOT hardcoded — so the defect is specific to `merge_evidence.py`'s coverage stats, not the whole coverage-gate surface. Separately, `plugins/dma-insights/skills/dma-assessment/SKILL.md` lines 5-6, 69, 152, 162, 433 all still say "17 categor[y/ies]" / "~836 subcapabilities" — confirmed live in the installed, in-scope plugin (not the legacy snapshot), so the wrong-universe description propagates into a second, separately-installed skill.

(2) The docstring's compaction assumption is FALSIFIED: I forced a real autocompact inside a `claude -p` run (three large docs/text/*.txt reads, --autocompact 100000) — debug log shows "autocompact: level=compact effectiveWindow=80000" and a forked [compact] summarizer agent — and then, in the same session, asked the model to recite the SessionStart routing brief verbatim; it answered "FORGOTTEN," explaining "Session-start hook output from a prior session does not persist into a fresh context window." No SessionStart:compact hook entry appears in that debug log at all — the brief is not reprinted and nothing else re-supplies it. This is PRESENT-DEFECTIVE (the suppression-on-compact logic is built on a false premise) compounding into ABSENT-UNNOTICED (no file in the repo names this as a known risk or open decision). (3) The DISPATCH-MODE preamble (agent_run.py lines 45-59, read in full) covers only connector-availability and output-format; it never mentions routing.md, and grepping all 47 agent definitions under plugins/dma-insights/agents/ for "routing.md" or "route before you produce" returns exactly 1 hit (orchestration/surface-producer.md) — so a dispatched agent is told how to report, never how to route, confirmed as stated. Stage 5 (per-subcap research + MECE diagnostic questions) audited against the owner-supplied v4.2 archive at /tmp/dmar/dma-research per §2.3(d) -- the installed plugins/dma-insights/skills/dma-research is version drift and was not used as the source of truth. All 12 checks were run as real commands/mutations against this archive, not read-and-assumed.

Headline: the KG build is genuinely well-engineered and its build-time gates are real (G1-G12 in validate_kg.py all mechanically fire and were proven to fire with real mutation tests). But every check that matters for UNATTENDED, per-engagement correctness -- as opposed to one-time KG construction -- turned out to be either (a) a build-time-only gate that never re-runs against the runtime-tailored artefact actually fired at a client, or (b) a self-graded LLM "challenge card" with zero independent script verification. In a headless architecture with no human and (per §1.2) no second model pass reviewing the first, self-graded checks are unenforced in practice.

Concretely, by ID:

S5-01 (within-subcap exhaustive/exclusive): NOT exhaustively enforced. `templates/schemas/evidence_item.schema.json` facts[].required = [fact_id,text,claim,subcaps,direction] -- `dq_facet` is NOT required (read at file lines 167-198). A fact can be ledgered with no facet tag at all. floors_gate.py:76 (`facets.setdefault(s_,set()).add(f.get("dq_facet"))`) then explicitly discards None (`- {None}` at line 98), so untagged facts simply don't count toward the facet_spread>=3 floor check -- they are neither rejected nor required to be reclassified. Exclusivity is schema-true (dq_facet is a single enum value, not a list) but nothing stops the same underlying claim being re-submitted as two separate `fact_id`s under two different facets -- no dedup-across-facets check exists anywhere in scripts/. PRESENT-DEFECTIVE (partial: mechanically exclusive per-fact, not exhaustive at all).

S5-02 (anti-clone guard, Rule 22): two DIFFERENT things share the "anti-clone" name here, and the trap is real. (1) The ONLY anti-clone code that exists is `validate_kg.py`'s W2 check (lines 39-46), which compares each subcap's **pre-built query TEMPLATE text** (`b["q"]["primary"]`) across siblings sharing a capability -- a KG-build-time-only check (confirmed: it's listed only under the "KG rebuilt"/"Install" QA rows in `references/protocols/cowork_project_prompt.md:166-168,308`, never under Batch/Category/Engagement rows). Reproduced live: cloning 3 siblings' `q.primary` and re-running `validate_kg.py` gave `WARN W2 query-clone clusters (>=3 siblings identical): 1` with **exit code 0** -- confirmed nothing stops; a WARN never fails the build gate (`sys.exit(1 if fails else 0)`), and no downstream script (`grep -rln clone scripts/engine scripts/deliver` -> zero hits) ever reads or acts on it. (2) The DOCUMENTED anti-clone guard everyone actually means at category-close -- "**>=3 siblings sharing >60% identical EVIDENCE ids**" (`references/protocols/safeguard_gates.md` SG-09, `cowork_project_prompt.md:118-119,184,288`) -- has **zero code implementation anywhere in the archive**. `grep -rn "60\b" scripts/` and `grep -rn sibling scripts/` return nothing relevant. It exists only as prose the LLM agent is instructed to self-police at "category close." This is the exact class of false-positive trap §2.3 warns about: a real, working, mechanically-verified W2 check exists for a narrowly-different object (query templates), which could be mistaken for coverage of the actually-documented SG-09 evidence-overlap guard, which does not exist in code. **ABSENT-UNNOTICED for SG-09's evidence-overlap form; PRESENT-DEFECTIVE (toothless WARN) for the W2 form that does exist.** In an unattended run, a category CAN and will close with smeared/cloned evidence with nothing stopping it.

PRESENT-SOUND (mechanism as designed; the "cannot both enter" framing in the audit brief does not describe how the system actually works and should not be treated as a defect).

S5-08 (volley-fired proof via floors_gate --require-synthesis, Rule 27/28): PRESENT-SOUND, proven with a live mutation, not just a read. S5-09 (contradicts as load-bearing facet / counter_evidence detectability): the contradicts facet's PRESENCE in every brief is structurally guaranteed (G7's canonical-order check forces it into every subcap's dq[3], confirmed at S5-07/S5-03). Whether it was actually FIRED and honestly assessed during a live engagement is a different question, and here the finding is starker than the prompt's own framing suggested: neither half of "q.negative never fired, or fired and a hit was ignored" (`references/protocols/challenge_protocol.md:17`) is mechanically checked in this codebase. `grep -n "negative\|NEGATIVE" scripts/engine/floors_gate.py scripts/engine/followup.py` shows those files only handle a DIFFERENT "negative" concept (`negative_finding` absence-claim ladders, R30) -- there is no check anywhere that the specific `q.negative` (NEGATIVE_Q = counter-evidence search template) was ever logged as fired for a subcap. The `counter_evidence` dimension is populated purely as a self-reported field inside a `kind:"verdict"` ledger record (see the golden test's own fixture at `tests/golden/integration_smoke.py` line ~64: `"counter_evidence":{"verdict":"CONCERN","delta":0}` -- hand-authored, not computed), and `ledger.py`/`build_handoff.py` only store and pass this through verbatim -- zero verification against the underlying search log. So: (a) "never fired" IS theoretically mechanizable (floors_gate already does an analogous proxy -- `csearch` -- for the *contradicts*-facet search, at line ~82-87) but is simply not implemented for q.negative specifically; (b) "fired and ignored" is not mechanizable without model judgment. **Both currently rely on the same model's own self-report, with no independent script catching either failure mode** -- worse than a 50/50 split. PRESENT-HUMAN-DEPENDENT in spirit (model-dependent, no reviewer) -- a BLOCKER per this audit's calibration, since it is exactly the "second model pass" §1.2 says does not exist.

S5-10 (facet-coverage lying check, synthesis_quality dim): NOT implemented as code anywhere. `grep -rn facet_coverage scripts/` returns exactly 3 hits, none of which validate content: `orient.py:59` (a STUB template), `build_handoff.py:59` and `populate_workbook.py:102` (both just copy the field through). In headless operation a synthesis can claim it checked contradicts and found nothing, without ever having actually searched, and nothing will catch the lie.

S5-11 (query fidelity sample, 20-30 subcaps / 4 pillars): sampled 28 subcaps (7 per pillar, deterministic seed) and read each one's works/fails DQ against its 3 pre-built `q.primary` queries. 24/28 (86%) plausible fidelity -- an answer to the queries would plausibly answer the DQ. **4/28 (14%) showed clear, reproducible drift**, each traced to root cause: (1) P1C2.1.4 "Role Definitions" -> query `"{e}" chief {kw} officer` renders literally as "chief role definitions officer" (not a real title) -- traced to `build_kg.py:100`'s EXISTS_FORMAL archetype template blindly inserting the subcap's own keyword into a C-suite-title search regardless of whether that concept plausibly has one; (2) P1C2.1.7 "Salesforce Platform Center of Excellence" -> query `"model salesforce 2025 2026"`, a garbled fragment unrelated to the DQ's actual ask (governance cadence of a CoE); (3) P4C1.9.RIA1 "...Multi-Custodian Data Integration & Householding" -> queries `"data sub-vertical unified"` / `"API data sub-vertical"` -- traced to `build_kg.py:56-58`'s STOP list not filtering the taxonomy meta-term "sub-vertical" (which appears in this subcap's boilerplate description), so `keyterms()` (line 60-63, ranks by raw frequency) surfaces a system term instead of "custodian"/"householding"; (4) P4C3.8.CIB1 "Corporate & Investment Banking: Payments & Treasury Integration" -> queries collapse to generic `"corporate investment unified"`, losing all Payments/Treasury specificity, returning to the same STOP/keyterms weakness on long compound names. Denominator: 4/28 sampled subcaps. **PRESENT-DEFECTIVE** -- root-caused, reproducible, and (given the shared template mechanism) generalizable beyond the sample.

S5-12 (map-fact mapping quality / TF-IDF semantic index): ran `scripts/build/semantic_index.py query()` against 10 realistic synthetic sweep-facts (deliberately written to mirror real evidence prose) spanning distinct subcaps. 9/10 (90%) top-1 hits were correct or a very close sibling. 1/10 produced a wrong top-1 mapping: a fact almost verbatim from P2C2.5.3 "Initial Funding Options"'s own fails-signal library ("...admits data re-keying between systems, CFPB complaint database shows rising complaints specifically citing...") returned `Commercial Loan Application` (0.178), `Loan Servicing & Modifications` (0.177), `Commercial Loan Servicing` (0.175) as its top 3, with the actually-correct P2C2.5.3 ranked 7th at 0.137 -- all scores clustered and low. Root cause, verified against `dq_generator._pick()` (scripts/build/dq_generator.py:41-49): the fails-signal library phrases are shared across many AUTOMATION-archetype subcaps' signal pools, so a fact phrased using that shared boilerplate has genuinely ambiguous TF-IDF discriminative weight -- the mapper cannot disambiguate it, and Rule 11's "one fetch -> many subcap facts" would propagate this exact mis-mapping across the taxonomy. Denominator: 1/10 sampled facts (small sample, but reproducibly demonstrated and root-caused). PRESENT-DEFECTIVE.

Overall Stage-5 verdict for headless viability: the KG's static structure and build-time gates (G1-G12, including the openness and facet-completeness checks) are genuinely sound and were proven to fail on real mutations. But every mechanism that would need to catch a problem DURING an unattended engagement -- anti-clone on live evidence (S5-02), tailoring enforcement (S5-04), the platform-agnostic guarantee against the artefact actually fired (S5-05), counter-evidence honesty (S5-09), and facet-coverage-lying detection (S5-10) -- is either absent or exists only as a self-graded LLM instruction with zero independent verification. This is the specific shape of risk unique to this stage: it looks rigorous (12 named gates, a 7-dimension challenge protocol, detailed rubric cards) while roughly half of that rigor is unenforced prose.

Stage 6's "challenge layer" is real as a self-report protocol validated for JSON-schema shape, but almost none of its actual judgment dimensions are independently computed. Audited against the OWNER-SUPPLIED v4.2 archive (/tmp/dmar/dma-research/), cross-checked against the live repo (apps/{api,mcp,worker,web}, packages/shared, migrations/, plugins/dma-insights/) per trap 2.3(d). Every claim below is a command I ran or a file:line I read, not an inference.

KEY RESULT: of the 12 named challenge dimensions (7 subcap: evidence_diversity, tier_hygiene, recency_decay, m_delta_fit, counter_evidence, precedence, synthesis_quality; 5 category: coverage_honesty, floor_compliance, conflict_resolution, single_source_concentration, theme_coherence), a grep across scripts/ (`for dim in ...; do grep -rl "$dim" scripts/; done`) found ZERO code implementations for 11 of 12 -- the one "precedence" hit (contingency.py, validate_kg.py, build_kg.py, build_handoff.py) is the unrelated KG dependency-graph concept, not the challenge dimension. All 12 dimensions are self-reported JSON from the SAME model that produced the research, validated only for enum membership (PASS/CONCERN/FAIL) by templates/schemas/challenge_verdict.schema.json -- never cross-checked against the underlying ledger. The "any FAIL => overall FAIL / >=2 CONCERN => CONCERN" arithmetic (challenge_protocol.md:21-22) exists only as an instruction to the self-challenging model; no script computes or verifies it.

What IS genuinely code-enforced (verified by running it, not just reading): (1) contingency.py's Stage-2a A-H classifier -- deterministic, ran it live twice with different inputs and got correct Case H / Case B outputs -- but it operates purely on self-reported strength/divergence fields. (2) floors_gate.py's length/punctuation heuristics for shallow_reading/no_deep_dive/so_what_missing -- empirically defeated with a 232-character, evidence-free, boilerplate sentence that satisfies every predicate (len>=180, ends in punctuation, >=25 spaces). (3) ledger.py's id-collision detector -- empirically forced a real collision (two `ledger.py append` calls, same evidence_id, different url) and confirmed compact() flags id_collisions:1, and floors_gate.py --require-synthesis genuinely exits 1 citing "LEDGER:evidence_id_collision:E-001(...)" -- but the compacted evidence_index.json had ALREADY silently overwritten the original evidence item's facts (last-write-wins) by the time the collision is flagged; recovery is a purely textual instruction to an agent, not automatic. (4) kg_reader.py's checksum guard -- empirically ran `guard --checkpoint <mismatched>` and confirmed `sys.exit("HALT R23: ...")` with the message going to stderr, exit 1, stdout empty, and nothing in routines.json / infra/ / scripts/ wired to catch or alert on a Cowork subprocess's nonzero exit (the four scheduled routines are unrelated Cloud Run Scheduler jobs for the package-scan/corpus-gate/pack-exporter/enrich-loop, and CLAUDE.md itself states the dma-surface-production scheduling automation "lands with stages 2-3" -- not yet built).

The self-challenge has no structural-independence guarantee. cowork_project_prompt.md's multi-agent matrix assigns "S1-S7 + challenge" to the SAME "Category Researcher" role, and subcap_challenge.yaml:6 literally instructs "You are challenging YOUR OWN findings." [every connector write tool]` and states "Independent of the fixer BY CONSTRUCTION... Both doors are closed by construction, in the front matter above, not by policy." The `provisional`/`ceiling_band_delta` flag DOES survive from the challenge card into research_handoff.json (empirically confirmed: ran tests/golden/integration_smoke.py end-to-end, output included `"challenge": "PASS"` in a subcap_record; build_handoff.py:68 writes `"PROVISIONAL"` when `v.get("provisional")` is true) -- but it dies immediately after. workbook_spec_v3.md's Subcap_Synthesis sheet has exactly 13 named columns (populate_workbook.py:94-96) and none is challenge/provisional. Circular corroboration (S6.2's named attack) is unguarded twice over: evidence_methodology.md:88-90 states the rule in prose ("Annual Report + Investor Deck are NOT independent... Annual Report + CFPB complaints ARE independent") but ers_v2.py:91 takes `--corroboration` as a required self-supplied float with no code checking source lineage, and the stated defense (`single_source_concentration`, counting domains) is itself one of the 11 unimplemented challenge dimensions -- so a vendor press release and a trade-press article quoting it (two different domains) would defeat both the stated defense and receive a self-assigned high corroboration score.

Stage 8 is the audit's largest confirmed net-new-build gap. The [LEAD] is TRUE and verified directly from source: `apps/mcp/server.py` has exactly 33 `@mcp.tool()` decorators (`grep -c "@mcp.tool()" apps/mcp/server.py` → 33) and zero of them, nor any other file under apps/api, apps/mcp, apps/worker, apps/web, packages, migrations, plugins, scripts, or infra, constructs or serves an .xlsx or .docx byte stream (`grep -rn "Workbook()\|\.save(" apps/worker apps/api apps/mcp packages migrations` → 0 matches outside embedding-model bootstrap in Dockerfiles). Promotion's atomic unit is fixed at six JSON pages only (`apps/mcp/dma_mcp/contracts.py:22 PAGES = ("heatmap","overview","insights","platform","context","techstack")`; `apps/mcp/dma_mcp/promote.py:186` checks `missing = [p for p in PAGES if p not in live]` against exactly those six) — there is no seventh slot for a workbook or report artefact anywhere in the writer registry or promote transaction. PRD explicitly scopes the workbook/report/evidence-index/package as "Unchanged by this product" (PRD line 66) and "Report, workbook and package files parsed. Read-only thereafter" (PRD line ~1229) — so the *absence* of a publish path is ABSENT-BY-DESIGN as far as "does this app author or re-emit the bytes" goes. findings_deduped.title: No cap on how many times a synthesis run may stall, lapse and be reclaimed; the same stall is independently re-recorded rather than escalated
findings_deduped.observed: apps/mcp/dma_mcp/claims.py provides a 90-minute claim TTL with silent takeover of a lapsed lease, but no attempt counter or quarantine equivalent to Stage-1 ingest's MAX_INGEST_ATTEMPTS=3. Live evidence: run bf3754b8 (Lawley) was recorded STALLED three separate times by the hourly watchdog (MEM-0267, MEM-0285, MEM-0306; all MAJOR, OPEN) within roughly one hour on 2026-08-25, each fix_hint saying only to wait for the lease to lapse.
findings_deduped.measurement: search_findings('watchdog observability trigger-fired session cannot be seen from outside') returned 3 distinct OPEN findings (MEM-0267, MEM-0285, MEM-0306) for the identical run_id bf3754b8 with defect_class PRODUCER_CLAIM_OUTLIVES_ITS_TURN, timestamped 2026-08-25T01:29Z, 08:29Z and 09:29Z respectively.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A run that keeps failing to complete for a structural reason (e.g. a recurring dispatch defect) cycles claim -> stall -> lapse -> reclaim indefinitely, generating a new fragmented finding on every hourly watchdog pass instead of one escalating signal, and never reaches a state anyone is forced to act on.

findings_deduped.title: A dropped-connection replay risk on the chunked payload transport is closed by a prompt instruction, not a server-side guard
findings_deduped.observed: ROUTINES.md warns producers never to resend an appending section after a RemoteDisconnected because 'resending an appending section duplicates its content.' apps/mcp/dma_mcp/transport.py protects a retried append_payload_part call at the same (upload_id, part) via ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, but nothing prevents a producer that believes a submit failed from opening a brand-new upload_id and re-appending the same cell_evidence items into a second, distinct assembled payload.
findings_deduped.measurement: Read apps/mcp/dma_mcp/transport.py:301-311 (per-part idempotency confirmed) and cross-checked against ROUTINES.md's dispatch-mode text: 'a submit that dies with RemoteDisconnected on a heavy page has usually SUCCEEDED server-side... never resend on a dropped connection alone' — a discipline instruction with no corresponding code-level guard against a fresh open_payload replaying the same content.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A producer session, uncertain whether its submit succeeded after a transport error, opens a new upload and resubmits the same heatmap section under a new submission id; both submissions independently pass validation and the later one is promoted, doubling cell_evidence content without any server-side detection.

findings_deduped.title: identifiers.find_fabricated() — the function the codebase built and unit-tested specifically to "reject a payload minting an evidence id" — is never called anywhere in production code
findings_deduped.observed: apps/mcp/dma_mcp/identifiers.py defines find_fabricated() (lines 57-68) with a module docstring claiming the four-namespace recogniser exists so a payload "minting" an evidence id is rejected. apps/mcp/tests/test_identifiers.py::test_mint_namespace_is_matched_and_fabrication_is_visible exercises it directly and passes. But grep across the whole live tree shows find_fabricated is referenced only inside identifiers.py itself and its own test file — no caller in validation.py, validation2.py, gates.py, or server.py. The actual invariant-10 rejection of a fabricated mint-namespace id in a submitted payload is instead implemented completely separately, via a DB round-trip (get_evidence/resolve_evidence_id) in validation2.py's citation walker (~line 3308), which raises gate ET-02 ("the mint namespace is server-allocated; an invented mint id is fabrication by construction") or ET-01 for other fabricated/foreign ids.
findings_deduped.measurement: `grep -rln "find_fabricated" /home/user/Accelerate` (excluding __pycache__ and a docs .txt) returns exactly 2 files: apps/mcp/dma_mcp/identifiers.py and apps/mcp/tests/test_identifiers.py. `python3 -m pytest apps/mcp/tests/test_identifiers.py -q` -> 5 passed (all in this file, none call the ET-01/ET-02 path).
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A maintainer trusting identifiers.py's own docstring ("reject a payload minting an evidence id" is this module's job) edits or removes find_fabricated() believing it is load-bearing for invariant 10, without realizing the real enforcement lives in validation2.py's separate DB-backed check — the invariant would keep working, but the documentation/implementation mismatch means nobody can trust this module's stated purpose.

findings_deduped.title: Gate A's transitive-import and dependency-manifest coverage is structurally incomplete (source-line regex only)

Checked apps/{api,mcp,worker}/requirements.txt and apps/web/package.json: none currently declare any blocklisted package, and a grep for raw HTTP calls to inference endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, generativelanguage.googleapis.com) across the four deployables returned zero hits — so there is no live violation today, only a narrower-than-implied guarantee.

findings_deduped.title: Audit baseline stale by one Python test
findings_deduped.observed: Prompt's cited baseline is 3,807 passed / 12 skipped; a clean, twice-repeated reproduction at HEAD gives 3,808 passed / 12 skipped with identical skip reasons.
findings_deduped.measurement: `python -m pytest apps/worker/tests/ apps/mcp/tests/ apps/api/tests/ scripts/tests/ plugins/dma-insights/scripts/tests/ tests/skills/ infra/jobs/tests/ -q -rs -rf` on a freshly migrated DB (108 tables), run twice, both '3808 passed, 12 skipped', 3820 collected.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: Anyone diffing future runs against the documented '3,807' will flag a false regression (or miss a real one) the moment the baseline is reproduced honestly; no failing or newly-skipped test is involved.

findings_deduped.title: Gate A (no-inference-imports) has no test and no negative control
findings_deduped.observed: Gate A enforces invariant 1 (no model calls at request time) but has zero test coverage anywhere in the repo.
findings_deduped.measurement: `ls scripts/tests/` contains no test_gate_a*.py; `grep -rln gate_a_no_inference_imports --include=*.py . | grep -v pycache` returns only scripts/gate_a_no_inference_imports.py itself.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A refactor changes how the gate detects a forbidden import (new alias, re-export path, lazy import); the gate stops catching real violations; CI stays green while an inference call reaches the serving path, and nothing in the suite would ever surface the regression.

findings_deduped.title: Gate K (rejections return) has no test and no negative control
findings_deduped.observed: Gate K enforces invariant 12's evidence-refusal visibility (a refused payload cannot be undetectable) but has zero test coverage anywhere.
findings_deduped.measurement: `ls scripts/tests/` contains no test_gate_k*.py; `grep -rln gate_k_rejections_return --include=*.py . | grep -v pycache` returns only the gate's own source file.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: The rejection ledger's wiring silently breaks (the gate's own CI comment describes exactly this happening three times in one day, found only by a human reading a verdict); Gate K has never been proven capable of catching its own failure mode.

findings_deduped.title: Gate M (evidence URL/span) is never invoked in the pipeline
findings_deduped.observed: Gate M was purpose-built after the owner found 85% of one client's served evidence had no URL, but it is called nowhere except its own unit test.
findings_deduped.measurement: `grep -rn gate_m_evidence_url_and_span --include=*.py --include=*.yml --include=*.sh .` (excluding __pycache__) returns exactly the gate's own source file and its own test's import — zero references in ci.yml, infra/deploy.sh, or infra/jobs/corpus_jobs/gate_scan.py.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: The exact defect Gate M was built to catch (a URL or verbatim-span field dropped in transit) recurs on a future client; nothing in CI, the nightly scanner, or deploy ever runs the check against real data, so it is never caught.

findings_deduped.title: Gates B, C, D, F have no test and no negative control
findings_deduped.observed: Corpus ceiling ratchet (B), no-render-dead-ends (C), shared-contracts-ship (D), and declared-keys-have-readers (F) all lack any test file; the repo's own scripts/mutation_check.py docstring calls C, D and F's negative control 'hand-checked... a habit, not a property', an acknowledged-but-unautomated gap; B is not mentioned there at all.
findings_deduped.measurement: `ls scripts/tests/` has no test_gate_{b,c,d,f}*.py; repo-wide grep for each module name outside its own gate_*.py source returns zero hits; scripts/mutation_check.py header names C, D, F among items only manually verified once.
findings_deduped.component: scripts/ (corpus governance, rendering, deploy image, contract-to-render census)
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: Any of the four incidents these gates were built to catch (corpus growing past its ratchet; an em-dash-style render dead end; a shared contract missing from the deploy image; a declared payload key with no reader) recurs after the detection logic silently drifts, and CI stays green because nothing proves these gates can still fail.

findings_deduped.title: Chunked-payload pagination boundary/offset arithmetic is mutation-unverified
findings_deduped.observed: get_staged_payload's part-boundary check (`part < 1 or part > total`) and byte offset (`(part - 1) * SECTION_INLINE_BYTES`) have surviving mutants — 3 of 6 sampled mutations are not caught by the suite.
findings_deduped.measurement: `python3 scripts/mutation_check.py --pairs` for the test_staged_readback.py pair: '3/6 mutants killed', survivors 'line 216: 1 -> 2', 'line 210: > -> >=', 'line 210: < -> <='.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: An off-by-one in the part-numbering boundary or byte-offset calculation ships silently (suite stays green); a client resubmitting a large section via this exact recovery path (added after a real 1.36MB-section loss) receives a truncated or misaligned chunk.

findings_deduped.title: One of the 12 CI skips is a code-shape gap, not an environment gap
findings_deduped.observed: 11 of 12 documented CI skips are genuinely credential/artefact-gated; the 12th (test_gap_false_positives.py's fallthrough test) self-skips because no current overview section has the field-map shape it needs, meaning that fallthrough branch of gaps_for_section has zero live coverage in any environment.
findings_deduped.measurement: apps/mcp/tests/test_gap_false_positives.py line ~89: `if not real: pytest.skip("every overview section wraps its fields today")`; confirmed present among the 12 SKIPPED lines in the reproduced run and confirmed by its own docstring to not be a database/credential skip.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A future contract section is authored with fields declared inline; if the `or spec` fallthrough has a latent bug, the gap worklist could silently report zero gaps for an incomplete section, and the one test guarding this exact branch has never actually executed its assertion.

findings_deduped.title: dma-assessment skill still builds a 17-category/836-subcap workbook against a settled 16/851 taxonomy
findings_deduped.observed: SKILL.md:69 requires a 17-row Category_Detail sheet and lines 152/158/433 use ~836 subcaps for query-volume math; catalogue is 851 cells / 16 categories.
findings_deduped.measurement: grep -n '17 categor|836 subcap' plugins/dma-insights/skills/dma-assessment/SKILL.md returned 6 hits (lines 5,6,69,152,162,433) against packages/shared/catalogue_v70_tier.json:31 '"cells": 851'.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A producer session run headless against dma-assessment SKILL.md builds a Category_Detail sheet with 17 rows and allocates research query budget for 836 subcaps; the workbook then structurally disagrees with the catalogue (851 cells, 16 categories) that the rest of the pipeline is built against, invisible until a contract/grain gate rejects it or, worse, silently accepts the wrong row count.

findings_deduped.title: MCP-TOOLS.md has no freshness check, unlike two of the three other generated artefacts examined
findings_deduped.observed: No CI step or test regenerates and diffs plugins/dma-insights/docs/MCP-TOOLS.md; it is in sync today only because no commit has touched apps/mcp/server.py since it was generated.
findings_deduped.measurement: diff of a fresh regen (python3 plugins/dma-insights/scripts/gen_mcp_tools_md.py . <tmp>) against the committed file showed only the stamped-commit line differing; git log 3e2d5e3bf9..b6de2dc737 -- apps/mcp/server.py = 0 commits; .github/workflows/ci.yml has exactly 1 generated-doc freshness step (docs/text), none for MCP-TOOLS.md.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A future PR adds or renames an MCP tool in apps/mcp/server.py without anyone re-running gen_mcp_tools_md.py; CI and the test suite both pass green because nothing checks the doc, and every producer/checker agent reading MCP-TOOLS.md for tool contracts works from a stale reference with no signal that it drifted.

findings_deduped.title: fixtures/reference_surface_keys.json generator has no automated freshness check
findings_deduped.observed: scripts/gen_reference_surface_keys.py's own docstring says the output is 'COMMITTED and reviewed' with no test regenerating and diffing it, unlike gen_customer_allowlist.py which is enforced by apps/api/tests/test_customer_allowlist.py.
findings_deduped.measurement: grep -rln reference_surface_keys apps/ scripts/ fixtures/ returned 3 hits, none a *_test.py or tests/ file; by contrast python3 -m pytest apps/api/tests/test_customer_allowlist.py -q returned '10 passed in 0.37s' for the sibling generator.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A reference client's staged payload changes (new keys promoted) without anyone re-running gen_reference_surface_keys.py; the derived allowlist silently continues to strip fields now legitimately served, or serves fields no reference client demonstrates, with no test catching the drift.

findings_deduped.title: Gate H checks only 25% of matching persistence-claim lines in the prompt corpus
findings_deduped.observed: Gate H's table-scoping rule requires both a field name and a table name backticked together; only 5 of 20 lines matching its own claim regex qualify, leaving 15 unscoped and unchecked by design.
findings_deduped.measurement: Instrumented gate_h_prompt_persistence_claims.claim_lines() over the same 47 .md files the gate itself scans: 20 lines matched vs. the gate's reported '5 table-scoped ... checked'; spot-checked 2 of the 15 unscoped lines (03-pages/3-insights.md:64,128) against apps/mcp/dma_mcp/writer_spec.json's insight_cards/insights_landscape column lists and found both still accurate today.
findings_deduped.component: gate H / prompt persistence claim checker
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A future schema/writer change removes column binding for one of the 15 currently-unscoped fields; the corresponding prompt claim goes stale exactly the way the original MEM-0001 incident did, and gate H reports clean because those lines were never in its checked set.

findings_deduped.title: No request-driven front door exists; the synthesis Routine only picks pre-ingested runs, never creates one
findings_deduped.observed: Both routine mechanisms (Cloud Scheduler cron in routines.json and CCR fresh-session-per-firing triggers in ROUTINES.md) fire on a fixed schedule with no per-firing request payload. run_gate.py's `pick`/`queue_order` select one already-INGESTED run from list_pending_runs; the owner ruling quoted in ROUTINES.md is 'no client named to be admitted.' The 33-tool DMA connector has no create-run/submit-request tool.
findings_deduped.measurement: live list_pending_runs returned 282 rows, all status INGESTED, none created by any request mechanism; run_gate.py lines 315-537 confirmed queue-only selection; connector tool roster (get_page_contract...ingest_reviewer_feedback) has no intake-write tool
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: An owner types a request into a Routine, or a Slack deal-desk message arrives; nothing in the live system converts either into a `runs` row or any tracked entity, so the request silently goes nowhere and no headless component can act on it or even report that it was received.

findings_deduped.title: Slack ingress is entirely unbuilt — no auth, authz, rate limiting, or replay protection to evaluate because there is no code
findings_deduped.observed: Zero SLACK_ environment variables, zero Slack secrets, zero rate-limiting code anywhere in the live tree.
findings_deduped.measurement: grep -rn 'SLACK_' apps/api apps/mcp apps/worker apps/web packages migrations plugins/dma-insights scripts infra = 0 hits; grep -rni 'rate.?limit|throttle' apps/api apps/mcp --include=*.py = 0 hits
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: If a Slack integration were bolted on ad hoc to unblock the pipeline, there is no existing authentication/authorization/rate-limit/replay scaffolding to reuse, so an untrusted Slack message could trigger an expensive autonomous job for anyone able to post in the channel, with no defense against replay or flooding.

findings_deduped.title: No alerting exists for a stuck/quarantined ingest; the only failure surface requires a human to look
findings_deduped.observed: _record_package_failure writes a DB row and a print() log line on quarantine; infra provisions only roles/monitoring.metricWriter with no alert policies or notification channels anywhere in infra/.
findings_deduped.measurement: job_main.py:220-223 (print-only quarantine log); infra/provision.sh:66 grants roles/monitoring.metricWriter; 0 hits for alert-policy/notification-channel in infra/provision.sh and infra/deploy.sh
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A package quarantines after 3 failed attempts (or the scan job itself starts failing) and, with no human watching a headless pipeline, the stuck request sits invisible indefinitely — the client never gets their assessment and nobody is told why.

findings_deduped.title: Charter-claimed GCS artefact-byte persistence is not implemented in the live worker
findings_deduped.observed: apps/worker/README.md and CLAUDE.md both state artefact bytes are staged to GCS as part of the package scan; no code in apps/worker performs this, and the dependency isn't even declared.
findings_deduped.measurement: 0 hits for storage.Client/google.cloud.storage/bucket in apps/worker/*.py; google-cloud-storage absent from apps/worker/requirements.txt; job_main.py:232 downloads into a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() that is deleted after parsing
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: Anyone relying on the charter's stated irreversibility ('GCS artefact bytes cannot be backfilled') to reason about data safety is reasoning about a step that does not exist; original source document bytes are not retained anywhere once parsing completes, so they cannot later be re-verified or re-parsed with an improved parser.

findings_deduped.title: The ingested tier's 'read-only once scanned' invariant is not enforced by database grant
findings_deduped.observed: Unlike the serving/staging boundary (grant-enforced: svc_api has no SELECT on staging tables), the ingested tier grants svc_worker full SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE.
findings_deduped.measurement: migrations/versions/0005_ingested_tier.py:252: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON {t} TO svc_worker, for every ingested-tier table
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A future bug or an unreviewed new intake path running as svc_worker could UPDATE or DELETE an already-ingested run's rows and the database would not stop it — the invariant depends entirely on every future writer remembering to behave, the exact failure mode the grant-enforced serving/staging boundary was designed to prevent.

findings_deduped.title: Production candidate-selection dedupes by entity, contradicting the connector's own tested request-grain rule
findings_deduped.observed: scripts/synthesis_queue.py's select() groups pending runs by _key(run)=display_id only (one run per entity, newest wins) and run_gate.py's _queue_ready() imports that selector as primary and, on any import failure, falls back to an inline copy of the exact same entity-grain rule (run_gate.py:372-378) — while apps/mcp/server.py's list_pending_runs computes duplicate_requests/surplus_runs by grouping on (display_id, request_id), and its own test test_the_grouping_key_is_the_request_not_the_entity (apps/mcp/tests/test_pending_runs_duplicates.py:56-65) exists specifically to forbid entity-grain grouping, stating 'grouping by entity would call those duplicates and send a producer to drop real work.'
findings_deduped.measurement: grep -n 'def _key' scripts/synthesis_queue.py -> line 76 'return run.get("display_id") or run.get("run_id")'; run_gate.py:372-378 fallback identical key; both scripts/tests/test_synthesis_queue.py (13 tests) and apps/mcp/tests/test_pending_runs_duplicates.py (5 tests) pass today ('python3 -m pytest ... -q' -> '13 passed'/'5 passed') while encoding opposite grouping assumptions for the same duplicate problem.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: An entity refreshed under a new request id (the documented 6-month refresh cadence, migrations 0031/0032) while its prior, genuinely different assessment is still pending synthesis has the older run permanently bucketed as 'superseded' by run_gate.py's walk and is never produced — a real client DMA silently disappears from the headless pipeline with nobody watching to notice, exactly the harm the connector's own test was written to prevent.

findings_deduped.title: Entity identity resolution has no cross-check beyond a name-slug match; a false merge of two institutions is invisible to the foreign-evidence gate
findings_deduped.observed: entities.display_id TEXT UNIQUE (migrations/versions/0005_ingested_tier.py:83) is the only identity key; persist_package's sole existing-entity lookup is 'SELECT id FROM entities WHERE display_id = %s' (persist.py:275) built from the manifest institution name via _slug(). The table also carries domain ('cheapest identity check in the system'), primary_regulator ('a mismatch is an identity error') and jurisdictions ('fastest contamination check available') columns, but none are ever read back for comparison anywhere in apps/worker, apps/mcp or apps/api.
findings_deduped.measurement: grep -rn 'domain|primary_regulator|jurisdictions' apps/worker/dma_worker/persist.py returns exactly 3 lines (63, 282, 286), all writes at entity-creation time; grep across apps/mcp and apps/api for a read/compare against entities.domain, .primary_regulator or .jurisdictions returns 0 matches.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: Two distinct real institutions whose names normalize to the same slug (plausible for common bank/credit-union names, and structurally exactly the named production case of two Drive folders both titled 'Corporate America Credit Union - DMA', apps/worker/job_main.py:107-113) collapse onto one entities.id; all evidence from either is then correctly scoped to that shared id, so get_evidence's foreign check (invariant 4) — which halts production on a foreign entity_id — structurally cannot detect the merge. Confirmed from static code; whether this specific case has already occurred in production is unconfirmed (BLOCKED: needs a live DB query, no gcloud/DB credentials available here).

findings_deduped.title: The stated twin/PENDING_REVIEW adjudication fallback ('a human or the worker dedup rules') has no automated half wired in, and no human is scheduled in this architecture
findings_deduped.observed: run_gate.py:53-59 documents G4's resolution path as 'a human or the worker dedup rules adjudicate first,' but dma_worker.dedup.pick_winner/Candidate — the only code implementing 'worker dedup rules' — is never imported by job_main.py or persist.py; its sole importer in the repo is the isolated unit test apps/worker/tests/test_stage_1_1_1_2.py. MEM-0159 (run_gate.py:390-397) additionally documents that a refused package is re-offered, re-gated, re-claimed and re-refused every firing because the gate never durably consults vetting history.
findings_deduped.measurement: grep -rln 'pick_winner' . --include=*.py returns 2 files: apps/worker/dma_worker/dedup.py (definition) and apps/worker/tests/test_stage_1_1_1_2.py (its only call site) — 0 occurrences in apps/worker/job_main.py or apps/worker/dma_worker/persist.py.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A genuinely unresolvable twin-entity or folder-name-only identity case is permanently refused for auto-pick every firing, with no scheduled human to perform the stated other half of adjudication (CLAUDE.md: synthesis sessions are scheduled by the app, not a human) and no requestor/ticket to route the ambiguity to — the client's DMA never synthesizes and nothing surfaces this as an actionable, addressed alert beyond a record_finding entry a rectifier might eventually read.
findings_deduped.defect_class_guess: process-gap / human-in-the-loop-required (PRESENT-HUMAN-DEPENDENT, a BLOCKER per this audit's own headless-architecture calibration)

findings_deduped.title: The documented 'four-signal entity cascade' is a three-signal cascade in production — the known-names cross-check never runs
findings_deduped.observed: entity_resolution.resolve()'s signal 3 (document_header, checked against a known_names registry) is fully implemented and unit-tested, but persist.py's only live call site hardcodes document_header=None.
findings_deduped.measurement: grep -n 'resolve(' apps/worker/dma_worker/persist.py -A6 shows the single call: manifest_identity=inst.get('name'), request_id=manifest.get('run_id'), document_header=None, folder_name=folder_display — document_header is never populated from any live source.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: The one signal built to resolve a report's own stated legal name against a maintained known-names registry (which could catch a name collision or resolve a trading-name variant correctly) never executes on a real package; identity falls straight from manifest/request_id to the lowest-confidence, always-PENDING_REVIEW folder-name signal with nothing exercised in between.

findings_deduped.title: MEM-0092's duplicate figure is stale in its stated denominator and has not shrunk across three independent re-measurements
findings_deduped.observed: Live re-measurement today (2026-08-28) via list_pending_runs returns duplicate_requests=101, surplus_runs=109 against 282 total pending runs — numerically identical duplicate/surplus counts to the 2026-08-19 snapshot hardcoded in apps/mcp/server.py and plugins/dma-insights/docs/DECISIONS.md ('109 of 287'), while the total pool has moved 287->282; a third, older hardcoded snapshot in scripts/synthesis_queue.py:6 still cites 2026-08-16's '286 runs, 171 entities, 105 duplicates.' None of the three self-updates.
findings_deduped.measurement: Tool result file /root/.claude/projects/-home-user-Accelerate/efa8fc94-fcad-50f6-b4fc-e5ab0bd63f5d/tool-results/mcp-plugin_dma-insights_connector-list_pending_runs-1787948836109.txt lines 3427-3428: '"duplicate_requests": 101' / '"surplus_runs": 109'; grep -c '"run_id"' on that file = 282 (vs the docstring's 287).
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: Works but fails silently: any session or report citing any one of these three hardcoded figures is citing a number already proven stale by a trivial re-run of list_pending_runs, and — more substantively — the duplicate backlog is not being drained over a 9-day window despite the charter's idempotency claim, because nothing in the live ingest path actually resolves duplicates (see the entity/request-grain finding above); the numbers are reported, not fixed.

findings_deduped.title: No evidence-mode / assessment-type concept anywhere in the authority chain
findings_deduped.observed: The Backend Schema's full 26-type enum catalogue (user_role_t ... dedup_branch_t) contains nothing evidence-mode-shaped, and grep for evidence_mode/assessment_type/PUBLIC-HYBRID-INTERNAL returns 0 hits across Backend Schema, TRD, Surface Specification, Implementation Plan, PRD and QA Report
findings_deduped.measurement: grep -ni "evidence_mode|assessment_type|PUBLIC.*HYBRID.*INTERNAL" over 7 docs/text/*.txt files = 0 matches in all 7
findings_deduped.component: docs/text/DMA Insights - Backend Schema.txt (+6 sibling authority docs)
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A run researched with confidential client-internal documents (HYBRID/INTERNAL) is stored, served and redacted through the exact same code path as a pure-public run; nothing in the schema or serving layer can even ask which kind a given run is, so no future safeguard can be built against it without first adding the column the whole authority chain currently omits

findings_deduped.title: Evidence-mode classification is decided by a human question with no headless answerer
findings_deduped.observed: Phase A0 of the owner-supplied v4.2 dma-research skill is 'scope questions (mode, offerings, evidence mode PUBLIC/INTERNAL/HYBRID)', asked interactively at the start of a 1-conversation phase before any research begins; the installed live dma-assessment skill's 00_parameters_template.json requires mode_rationale, mode_confirmation_date and confirmed_by: '[User Name or Role]'; no routine in plugins/dma-insights/routines.json, and no script checked under scripts/, supplies or infers this value
findings_deduped.measurement: SKILL.md line 80 text quoted verbatim; 00_parameters_template.json lines 26-30 quoted verbatim; plugins/dma-insights/routines.json's 4 entries (dmai-package-scan, dmai-corpus-gate-scanner, dmai-pack-exporter, dmai-enrich-loop) checked, 0 carry an evidence_mode parameter or fire dma-research/dma-surface-production
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A Routine fires a headless session against dma-research per the CLAUDE.md-adjudicated scheduling model; the session reaches Phase A0 with nobody to answer, and either stalls indefinitely or a coding agent guesses a mode with no ground truth, silently mis-classifying internal-evidence runs as PUBLIC (or vice versa) with no downstream check able to catch it since the field does not exist in the schema at all

findings_deduped.title: Directory route hardcodes data_source instead of deriving it, and the value will become false
findings_deduped.observed: Every entity and every run object built in the live (non-proto) directory-listing route is assigned the literal string "data_source": "DRIVE_PARSE" unconditionally, not read from any column
findings_deduped.measurement: apps/api/dma_api/main.py:228 (entity dict) and :258-259 (run dict) both hardcode data_source: "DRIVE_PARSE"; grep -n data_source apps/api/dma_api/main.py = 2 occurrences, both string literals with no branching
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: Once the Drive-watching intake is retired per the charter's target architecture (Slack/Routine front door), every run created through the new path still reports data_source: "DRIVE_PARSE" on the client-facing directory, which is a default that looks like data (violates invariant 9) and could mislead a reader auditing how a given run's evidence was sourced

findings_deduped.title: Trap 2.3(c) confirmed distinct: posture_basis is not Stage-3 evidence mode
findings_deduped.observed: posture_basis (EVIDENCE|HYBRID|INFERRED) is documented in-code as 'a chip on a payload field, not prose' — a per-field posture indicator, unrelated to the run-level PUBLIC/HYBRID/INTERNAL classification
findings_deduped.measurement: apps/mcp/dma_mcp/gates.py:719 quoted verbatim: 'posture_basis is the EVIDENCE|HYBRID|INFERRED chip, not prose.'
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: None — this is a trap-verification entry confirming the [LEAD]'s caution was correctly heeded, not a defect in the live system

findings_deduped.title: No automated ingest path exists for internal documents; only a human-typed citation channel
findings_deduped.observed: apps/worker/dma_worker/classification.py's ARTEFACT_REGISTRY recognises only 6 file kinds (workbook, assessment_report.docx, client_profile.docx, manifest, structured json/csv exports, ops_sheet); job_main.py's drive.download() only ever fetches those. A raw internal document (board minutes, internal memo, RFP) dropped in the intake folder is classified None and never parsed. The only channel for internal facts is a human typing an INT-{label} id and excerpt into the workbook by hand.
findings_deduped.measurement: 0 of 25,537 evidence_index rows carry origin='internal' in production, measured 2026-08-09 and quoted verbatim in apps/api/tests/test_computed_at_read.py:293-298 (25,385 package + 152 producer + 0 internal).
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A Routine fires an unattended synthesis run for a client whose engagement is HYBRID/INTERNAL. No component of the pipeline can read the client's internal documents; the run either silently proceeds as if PUBLIC-only (thinner assessment, unflagged) or stalls waiting on a human step that the target architecture has removed.

findings_deduped.title: evidence_index.origin is never consulted by the redaction walker
findings_deduped.observed: redaction.py strips only producer-authored internal_only JSON paths and cohort entity_ids; it has zero references to the origin column. If internal-origin evidence ever begins flowing (source_url-less, INT-{label} ids), nothing automatically prevents its source_name/excerpt from reaching a customer-audience payload unless the producer separately, manually lists that JSON path in internal_only.
findings_deduped.measurement: grep -n 'origin' apps/api/dma_api/redaction.py returns 0 of 0 matches (empty result) against a 600+ line module that otherwise implements the full invariant-5 walker.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: If internal-document ingest (finding above) is ever built without also wiring origin-based redaction, the first internal-origin evidence item cited on a customer-visible card leaks provenance/content that was never meant to cross the audience boundary, because no server-side control currently keys off origin.

findings_deduped.title: Source-URL-less (internal) citations bypass verbatim verification by construction, and are auto-downgraded to INFERENCE
findings_deduped.observed: register_evidence()'s fetch-and-verify block is gated entirely on `if source_url:` — absent for internal documents. A FACT claim with no source_url is silently rewritten to INFERENCE rather than rejected. This is deliberate and covered by a passing test, but it means invariant 4's excerpt requirement is enforced only structurally (length 50-500) for internal citations, never against the actual source.
findings_deduped.measurement: apps/mcp/dma_mcp/register.py lines ~194-219; test asserts the exact behaviour at apps/mcp/tests/test_register_evidence.py:131-142 (claim=='INFERENCE', identity_ok is None).
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: An internal document is misquoted or fabricated by a producer agent; since it has never actually occurred in production (0/25,537) this is latent, but the gate as designed would not catch a fabricated internal excerpt the way it catches a fabricated web excerpt.

findings_deduped.title: No credential anywhere in the repo opens an internal document in an unattended run
findings_deduped.observed: plugins/dma-insights/docs/secrets.md documents exactly two credential types (MCP path token, Google-signed connector ID token) and explicitly enumerates what is NOT present (no DB password, no Anthropic/Clay key) without ever mentioning internal-document access. The worker's Drive token is scoped only to the recognised artefact kinds.
findings_deduped.measurement: secrets.md, 158 lines, sections 1/1b/2/3 read in full; §3 'What is deliberately NOT here' (lines 140-147) lists 3 excluded credential classes, none of them internal-document access.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A headless Routine needs to incorporate a client's internal document; there is no service identity that can open it, so the step either silently never happens (facts missing, unflagged) or a human must do it out of band, which is the exact human dependency the target architecture has no room for.

findings_deduped.title: Counter-evidence and facet-coverage-honesty checks are self-graded by the same researching model with no independent script verification
findings_deduped.observed: The 7-dimension self-challenge protocol's counter_evidence and synthesis_quality dimensions (including the specifically-praised 'facet_coverage claims contradict the ledger' catch) are written as instructions in references/cards/*.yaml for the researching LLM to grade itself against; no script in scripts/engine or scripts/deliver cross-checks these claims against the actual search/evidence ledger.
findings_deduped.measurement: grep for facet_coverage in scripts/ returns only a stub (orient.py:59) and pass-through copies (build_handoff.py:59, populate_workbook.py:102); grep for q.negative firing checks in floors_gate.py/followup.py returns none; the golden test's own 'verdict' ledger fixture is hand-authored, not computed.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: In a headless run with a single model performing both research and self-challenge, a synthesis can assert 'contradicts: checked_none_found' or 'counter_evidence: PASS' without ever having actually run the counter-evidence search, and nothing independent will catch the false attestation before it reaches the client-facing report.
findings_deduped.defect_class_guess: present-human-dependent (no second reviewer exists in target architecture)

findings_deduped.title: Pre-built query templates drift from their diagnostic questions for a reproducible, generalizable subset of subcaps
findings_deduped.observed: Sampled 28 subcaps across all 4 pillars; 4 (14%) had pre-built queries that would not actually answer their own diagnostic question, traced to two template bugs: the EXISTS_FORMAL archetype's 'chief {kw} officer' query template firing regardless of whether the concept plausibly has a C-suite title, and a STOP-word list that fails to filter the taxonomy meta-term 'sub-vertical', letting it dominate keyword extraction over the subcap's actual distinguishing terms on long/compound names.

findings_deduped.title: Circular corroboration is unguarded by any code, and the one stated defense is itself unimplemented
findings_deduped.observed: The independence rule ('vendor PR + trade press quoting it are not independent') exists only as prose; corroboration_score is a required self-supplied CLI float with no lineage check, and single_source_concentration (the stated category-level defense) has zero code implementation.

findings_deduped.title: An id-collision under the fcntl allocator destroys the earlier evidence item's data in the same operation that detects it
findings_deduped.observed: Forcing a collision (two ledger.py append calls with the same evidence_id, different url) causes ledger.compact() to overwrite the earlier item (last-write-wins) while simultaneously flagging id_collisions:1, which correctly fails floors_gate.py's gate. But the fix is a purely textual do_first instruction for an agent — no automatic repair.
findings_deduped.measurement: Empirical run: `ledger.py append` (collision) -> `ledger.py compact` -> `{"id_collisions": 1, ...}` -> `floors_gate.py --require-synthesis` -> `gate: FAIL`, dq_gaps contains `LEDGER:evidence_id_collision:E-001(...)`, exit=1; direct read of evidence_index.json afterward shows E-001's facts:[] (original TestFCU facts gone).
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: If concurrent Category Researcher sub-agents ever run on more than one host (the archive states no single-host guarantee), a genuine id race destroys evidence data that only a human/agent noticing the do_first list can restore from the raw append-only ledger — in a fully unattended run, nothing forces that restoration to happen before promotion.

findings_deduped.title: qa_auditor.py always FAILs every canonical workbook regardless of quality, because it checks a schema the practice's own skill forbids
findings_deduped.observed: qa_auditor.py hardcodes sheet name f'{pillar}_Scoring_Detail' (the legacy 22-column A-V layout) at lines 117, 151, 210, 251, 314, 362. The canonical, SKILL.md-mandated layout is P#_Subcap_Scoring (11 columns). Ran qa_auditor.py --workbook against a synthetic well-formed canonical workbook (varied scores, unique evidence, full-length rationales) and against a deliberately bad one: both produced byte-identical issue_register.csv (4 CRITICAL rows, 'Missing sheet: P1/P2/P3/P4_Scoring_Detail'), identical qa_verdict.json (verdict:FAIL), and identical real process exit code 1. Internal log line 'QA audit complete: 0/0 checks passed' on both runs confirms score_bounds/evidence_linkage/caps_log_consistency/rationale_quality/weight_sums never executed.
findings_deduped.measurement: cd scratchpad && python3 qa_auditor.py --workbook good_workbook.xlsx --out-dir qa_out_good2 >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $? -> 1 (same as the deliberately bad workbook run); grep -c Scoring_Detail plugins/dma-insights/skills/dma-assessment/scripts/qa_auditor.py -> 6 occurrences, vs 0 occurrences of P#_Subcap_Scoring anywhere in that file
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: In a headless pipeline gating promotion/delivery on qa_auditor.py's exit code, EVERY real assessment workbook is refused unconditionally (false-FAIL on 100% of canonical inputs), OR — the likelier operational outcome given the tool is documented as mandatory — someone silences/ignores its result, in which case a workbook ships to a client with zero of its 6 real quality checks (score bounds 1.0-5.0, evidence-linkage-per-score, caps-log consistency, rationale length/evidence-citation, weight-sum-to-1.0) ever having run, silently, with no human present to notice the tool never actually looked at the data.

findings_deduped.measurement: mcp__plugin_dma-insights_connector__explain_gate(gate_id='G14') -> {"error": "unknown_gate", "gate_id": "G14"}; grep -noE '\"(AG|SG|ET|CG)-?[0-9]+\"' apps/mcp/dma_mcp/gates.py | sort -u shows 60 real ids, none bare-G; grep -rln uncertainty_band apps/mcp apps/api apps/worker --include='*.py' -> 0 files
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A synthesis agent can assert any ceiling and any uncertainty band on overview.ceilings — including one that grossly overstates confidence relative to its evidence tier — and no automated gate will refuse it before it reaches a client, because the contract names an enforcement mechanism ('G14') that does not exist.

findings_deduped.title: peer_median is verified-and-not-stored at ingest tier but stored-and-unverified at serving tier
findings_deduped.observed: apps/worker/dma_worker/persist.py:696-715 correctly implements invariant 8 for the ingested workbook artifact: raw per-peer scores go into peer_scores, and a stated median is recomputed and compared at 0.005 tolerance, with the comment 'stated value not stored'. But the SERVED peer_median (subcap_scores.peer_median, overview_findings.peer_median — plain stored NUMERIC(4,2) columns per migrations 0005/0008/0027) is written directly from the synthesis agent's submitted payload (apps/mcp/dma_mcp/promote.py has zero references to peer_median or peer_scores), and the only connector-side check (CG-44, gates.py/validation2.py) verifies internal arithmetic (delta = score - peer_median) and cross-page cascade, never that peer_median itself matches a real median of that run's peer_scores rows.
findings_deduped.measurement: grep -n peer_median apps/mcp/dma_mcp/promote.py -> 0 hits; migrations/versions/0011_peer_scores_category_grain.py:1-8 states the intended design ('medians...recompute downstream... counts are computed, never stored') which the serving tier does not follow for peer_median specifically
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A synthesis agent misreads or miscalculates a peer cohort median and asserts a wrong figure in the payload; CG-44 only checks that the delta subtracts correctly from whatever peer_median was asserted, so an internally-consistent but factually wrong peer comparison ships to the client with no gate catching it.
