findings_deduped.title: promote_run's retained-page re-validation skips pass2 (evidence/foreign-id) gates entirely
findings_deduped.observed: promote.py only imports and calls validate_pass1(page, payload) when re-checking a retained PASS submission before re-promotion; it never calls validate_pass2(conn, run_id, page, payload) or get_evidence, so ET-01/ET-02 (evidence resolution, foreign-id detection) are never re-asserted for retained rows at promote time — only at original submit time.
findings_deduped.measurement: grep -n 'validate_pass2|get_evidence' apps/mcp/dma_mcp/promote.py returns 0 of 574 lines; contrast with apps/mcp/dma_mcp/submit.py:230,236 which calls both validate_pass1 and validate_pass2 on every submit. apps/mcp/tests/test_promote.py has no test exercising an evidence/ET gate at re-promotion time (grepped for 'pass2|foreign' in that file: 0 matches), versus a dedicated CG re-validation test (test_a_retained_pass_that_fails_a_current_gate_refuses, using CG-09) and a dedicated SG-disclosure test — the evidence/ET path is the one family with no re-promotion test at all.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: A page is submitted and passes with a cited evidence id that later becomes foreign to the entity (e.g. a subsequent dedup/merge correction, or a data-quality fix reassigns the evidence row's entity linkage). The page's submissions row still carries superseded_at IS NULL and status=PASS. On any later re-promotion of that run (e.g. fixing one of the other five pages per the retention workflow), promote_run re-validates only pass1/CG and finds nothing wrong, so the stale page with the now-foreign citation is rewritten to the serving tables again — despite CLAUDE.md invariant 4 ('foreign halts production') and this section's own charter line ('a failing evidence reason never promotes') applying only at the original submit, not at every re-promotion the retained row survives.

findings_deduped.title: verify_deployed.py --quick silently reports a clean deploy when gcloud is unreachable
findings_deduped.observed: Running verify_deployed.py --quick with no gcloud CLI present exits 0 and prints 'No service has unshipped commits touching its source' even though every service's revision lookup failed with 'COULD NOT READ'. The full (non-quick) mode correctly refuses with exit 2 ('comparison NOT made... that is NOT a pass') in the identical environment.
findings_deduped.measurement: Ran `python3 scripts/verify_deployed.py --quick` (no gcloud installed): output showed 'dmai-web COULD NOT READ — [Errno 2] No such file or directory' for all 3 services, immediately followed by 'No service has unshipped commits touching its source... ' and exit code 0. Ran `python3 scripts/verify_deployed.py` (same environment, no --quick): exited 2 with 'Could not read the web image digest — comparison NOT made. That is not a pass.' Root cause at verify_deployed.py:81-84: `changed_since(built_at, paths)` returns `[]` when `built_at` is falsy, and the except-handler at line ~172-177 sets built_at='' on any read failure — so an unreadable service is indistinguishable from an up-to-date one in --quick mode only.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: Anyone running `verify_deployed.py --quick` by hand as a fast sanity check during a credential outage, a misconfigured gcloud context, or a wrong GCP_PROJECT/GCP_REGION env var gets a false 'all clear' instead of a refusal — the exact silent-failure shape the script's own docstring says it exists to end ('the only check was memory, and memory reported success'). Confirmed low blast radius: neither infra/deploy.sh nor .github/workflows/ci.yml ever pass --quick, so the production deploy path itself is not exposed to this defect.

findings_deduped.title: runs.status has no terminal 'final' value; three of six declared enum states (CLAIMED, SYNTHESISING, STAGED) are never written by any live code path
findings_deduped.observed: run_status_t is declared with 6 values (INGESTED, CLAIMED, SYNTHESISING, STAGED, PROMOTED, SUPERSEDED) in migrations/versions/0002_enumerated_types.py and documented identically in the Backend Schema doc, but grepping every `SET status` write against the runs table in apps/mcp and apps/worker (excluding tests) finds only PROMOTED (promote.py), SUPERSEDED/INGESTED-reset (migration 0032), and WITHDRAWN (withdraw.py) ever written. claims.py's claim_run never touches runs.status. So a run sits at INGESTED for its entire in-progress lifetime and jumps directly to PROMOTED; CLAIMED/SYNTHESISING/STAGED are vestigial. Separately, TRD.txt explicitly documents promotion as non-terminal ('Never. Promotion swaps is_active; nothing is deleted' — a later run always supersedes), and withdraw_run can revoke a promoted run at any time — so nothing in the schema or code ever marks a DMA as permanently done.
findings_deduped.measurement: grep -rn "SET status" apps/mcp/dma_mcp/*.py apps/worker/**/*.py migrations/versions/*.py (excluding *test*) → 4 files, 5 statements total, none setting CLAIMED/SYNTHESISING/STAGED. grep -n 'CLAIMED|SYNTHESISING|STAGED' apps/mcp/dma_mcp/claims.py apps/mcp/dma_mcp/submit.py → 0 of 2 files matched. grep -n 'terminal state|assessment complete|DMA final' across docs/text/*.txt (8 design docs) → 0 occurrences.
findings_deduped.failure_scenario: Not a correctness bug on its own (documented lineage design intentionally allows re-assessment forever), but it is a documentation-to-reality gap: anyone reading the Backend Schema's run_status_t list would reasonably expect a run's status to visibly progress through CLAIMED -> SYNTHESISING -> STAGED as a producer session works, and to use that progression to distinguish 'actively being worked' from 'stalled/abandoned' — but no signal exists at the runs.status level to tell those apart; a run stuck in INGESTED for months (session died mid-synthesis) looks identical in runs.status to one that was never touched, and the only staleness signal that exists at all is the run_claims lease expiry (claims.py), which is not surfaced by runs.status and is silently reclaimable rather than reported as an anomaly.

refuted_leads.lead: Section 4.1 framed as an open question: 'establish whether claude -p --agent ... loads plugin hooks at all' in a headless, trigger-fired session -- implying this might not work.
refuted_leads.how_refuted: Directly tested with the real installed claude CLI (v2.1.251) and the real installed plugin (dma-insights@zennify-dma v0.6.8): `claude -p "..." --agent dma-insights:qa-overseer --permission-mode dontAsk --debug hooks` produced debug log entries 'Registered 8 hooks from 1 plugins' and 'Hook SessionStart:startup (SessionStart) success:\ndma-insights: route before you produce...' -- the hook fires and its output reaches the model in exactly the invocation shape agent_run.py uses. The mechanism works; the actual defect (see findings) is downstream, at compaction, not at headless startup.

refuted_leads.lead: The audit text's 'contradiction that matters most' -- a missing register row and a confirmed-absent one both produce greenfield, so the engine cannot distinguish 'we know it is not there' from 'we never looked.'
refuted_leads.how_refuted: Ran apps/mcp/dma_mcp/fit.py's platform_fit() directly with (a) zero techstack rows at all and (b) one explicit status:'ABSENT' row for the same three cells. Result: Greenfield-family factor = 0.0 (fit_score 46.6) for the missing case vs 1.0 (fit_score 53.0) for the confirmed-absent case -- a reproducible, code-verified distinction. Corroborated by two passing tests in apps/mcp/tests/test_platform_fit_gate.py (lines 350-362, 404-411). The engine's design is conservative in exactly the direction that matters: an unscanned family never earns the greenfield bonus, so the feared systematic over-recommendation of unscanned estate does not occur through this path. A milder residual gap remains and is reported separately: when only one specific candidate's area (not the whole register) was never scanned, the run-level context.notes disclosure does not fire, so a reader of that one card cannot always tell 'confirmed present' from 'never looked' -- but the SCORE itself does not misrepresent it as greenfield.

refuted_leads.lead: An unmapped readiness phrase reads RED while an absent one reads amber (stated as something to verify inside check 4.6-09).
refuted_leads.how_refuted: Ran apps/mcp/dma_mcp/fit.py's _readiness_token() directly: unmapped phrase ('SOMETHING WEIRD') -> 'red' (true, matches the claim), but an absent/None readiness -> 'green', not 'amber' (false). Confirmed as the intended, tested behaviour via apps/mcp/tests/test_platform_fit_gate.py::test_an_absent_readiness_is_green_because_nothing_was_claimed, which passes. The premise in the check text is half right and half wrong; the wrong half (absent reads green, not amber) is reported as its own PRESENT-DEFECTIVE finding above because it contradicts the shared engine's own documented design rationale.

refuted_leads.lead: A search of the live tree for evidence_mode appears to return nothing (Stage 3 audit prompt, citing only apps/dma-insights/ as the source)
refuted_leads.how_refuted: grep -rn evidence_mode across apps/web (which is a live target directory per trap 2.3(a), not the legacy snapshot) finds it in apps/web/proto/{pages-d1-overview.jsx,pages-d5-d6-tech-runs.jsx,data.js}, apps/web/public/proto/js/*.js, and 9 files under apps/web/tests/*.test.js -- so the literal claim of zero hits in the live tree is false. The substance survives, though: all of these are prototype mock data or render-test fixtures (CLAUDE.md restricts prototype authority to layout/rendering, never data-fetch logic), and zero hits were found in apps/api, apps/mcp, apps/worker, packages/shared or migrations -- so no real serving-layer classification exists, which is what the lead was actually driving at.

refuted_leads.lead: S7-04's check text implies scripts/gate_j_surface_parity.py is (or should be read as) the mechanism enforcing the 0.05 grain tolerance across pillar/category/cell.
refuted_leads.how_refuted: Read the script in full (213 lines). Its own docstring is explicit and repeated: 'It never compares VALUES... Only the SHAPE of what is served is comparable' and it compares two DIFFERENT CLIENTS' payloads for structural parity (section/key presence), not one run's internal pillar-category-cell arithmetic. The actual 0.05-tolerance grain reconciliation is implemented in apps/mcp/dma_mcp/validation2.py's _served_figures() (backing gate CG-07) and gates.py's CG-07/CG-08/CG-30/CG-31/CG-44, all separately confirmed live via test_served_grain_rollup.py (4/4 passed) and test_validation_pass2.py (grain_lock and band tests passed against a real local Postgres).

The lead stands as verified fact, not merely a hypothesis.
